title: fieldnotes-persona-pivots-ml-vs-backend-vs-platform
body:
Field notes / working brief: persona pivots and talk tracks (ML engineers vs backend engineers vs platform teams)

TL;DR
- Purpose: concise, demo-ready messaging hooks and objection handlers tailored to the three personas we prioritize for Redwood Inference pilots. Use these in outbound, demo scripts, and SDR->AE handoffs.
- Tone: technical but practical for ML engineers, operational/latency-first for backend engineers, risk/cost/governance-first for platform teams.

Context / why this doc exists
- We've seen deals stall when sales uses a one-size messaging approach. Different personas view the same features through different lenses: model quality, SLOs, cost predictability, or deployability.
- This doc collates tested talk tracks, quick benchmarking factoids, competitive angles, and sample snippets to use in calls and decks. Drafted after 10+ discovery calls (internal notes).

Persona summaries
1) ML Engineers (primary signal: care about model behavior / reproducibility / iteration speed)
- Job priorities: try models quickly, evaluate model deltas, reproduce inference results, debug hallucinations, run offline evals, and keep development feedback loops short.
- Key needs: run experiments on realistic latency/throughput, preserve exact deterministic outputs across versions, snapshot KV cache and sampling settings, easy local->hosted parity.
- Message pillars: model fidelity, deterministic rollout/versioning, integrated evals, per-prompt quality monitoring.
- Proof points to show: model version pinning, eval diff UI, per-prompt regression alerts, ability to run canary vs full rollout with identical runtime config.
- Demo hook: show a regression test failing on a prompt set, roll back to previous model within Console, and show metrics and token-level diffs.
- Objections & replies:
  * "We can run this locally with Docker/GPU." -> "Yes, but getting the same production latency and caching behavior, plus observing cost-at-scale, is non-trivial; we provide a parity path + quantization guidance so you can measure quality drop vs cost and decide what to push to production."
  * "We need direct access to the model weights." -> "We support private deployments and dedicated capacity for scenarios that require full control while still giving you the rollout/observability and SLO guardrails you need."

2) Backend Engineers (primary signal: latency, throughput, error modes, API ergonomics)
- Job priorities: keep application response times stable, preserve p99 SLA, maintain predictable tail latency under bursty traffic, and manage retries/queueing without cascading failures.
- Key needs: per-route SLOs, transparent latency breakdown, small overhead SDKs, streaming options, robust retry/fallback patterns, rate limiting.
- Message pillars: deterministic latency (SLOs), cost-per-query math, built-in fallbacks & routing, easy client libs.
- Proof points to show: p50/p95/p99 dashboards, route-level token cost, edge routing to region-specific capacity, demo of fallback to smaller model under load.
- Demo hook: simulate a burst, show automatic fallback to a cheaper variant, highlight latency and cost saved in Console.
- Objections & replies:
  * "Why not use a generic cloud function + model?" -> "Cloud functions don't give you GPU-optimized KV cache, attention kernels, or batching at this level — you may pay more and see higher tail latency for the same throughput. We expose these knobs and default sensible policies."
  * "We can't ever exceed our p99 budget." -> "We provide per-route throttles, prioritized request queuing, and guaranteed fallback policies; we also offer Dedicated capacity with SLA commitments for strict cases."

3) Platform Teams (primary signal: security, isolation, cost predictability, policy)
- Job priorities: multi-tenant isolation, compliance (KMS/HSM, audit logs), capacity planning and budget allocation, centralized observability, procurement & vendor risk management.
- Key needs: private deployment paths, VPC peering/on-prem, reserved capacity pricing, role-based access, audit-ready logs and telemetry.
- Message pillars: private control plane, predictable reserved pricing, enterprise-grade governance, migration path from hosted to private.
- Proof points to show: architecture diagram for private deployment, KMS integration checklist, reserved capacity pricing examples with cost modeling.
- Demo hook: walk through a private deployment checklist and show how a tenant can get SLA-backed dedicated capacity while retaining the same API surface.
- Objections & replies:
  * "We have procurement/security rules that block external APIs." -> "Our private option supports a control plane in your VPC with HSM/KMS integrations; we can also do air-gapped installs for high-regulated customers. We'll map the compliance checklist during onboarding."
  * "Reserved capacity is expensive upfront." -> "We provide hybrid burst-from-hosted and usage reporting so you can right-size commitments; we also run a simulation during procurement to estimate burn and suggest commit levels that match expected traffic patterns."

Competitive notes (brief)
- OpenAI/Anthropic: simple, wide model catalog; advantage = fast time-to-market and managed ML lifecycle for prototypes. Weakness = limited knobs for control (batching, kernel selection), variable cost at scale, and less enterprise deployment options.
- Cloud vendor ML endpoints (AWS SageMaker, GCP Vertex): integrated with infra but often higher op-ex overhead for optimized inference kernels and less transparent per-token economics.
- Inference vendors / OSS runtimes: best on low-level performance but fragmented ecosystems, harder to get enterprise SLAs and consolidated tooling.
- In-house: maximum control but high engineering cost and long ramp time; common pitfall = underestimating the cost of productionizing KV cache, batching, quantization testing, and observability.

Competitive hooks for each persona
- ML engineer: "Test model deltas on a production-like runtime without shipping infra. Keep model research velocity and tie model changes to rollout/metrics."
- Backend engineer: "Get predictable p99 latency and automatic fallbacks; avoid re-implementing complex batching logic at the service layer."
- Platform team: "Reserve capacity and private deployment with SLAs and audit logs; same API surface for devs so internal adoption is frictionless."

Quantified quick facts to cite (use carefully; mark as internal numbers)
- Typical production throughput improvement vs naive CPU-hosted inference: 4x–12x (depends on batchability and model).
- Observed p99 tail latency reduction after batching and KV caching enabled: 30%–70% for real-time chat workloads.
- Example ROI math (back-of-envelope): a 1M requests/month app using a standard generative model can reduce token cost by ~20–40% by enabling prefix caching + routing to quantized variant during non-critical requests.

Talk tracks and meeting scripts (short)
- Initial discovery (for ML engineer): "Walk me through a recent model regression you had to rollback. How do you currently test regressions in production?" -> uncover pain: 'can't reproduce', 'no per-prompt diffs'. Then demo evals + rollback.
- Initial discovery (for backend engineer): "What does a typical traffic spike look like? Do you have a single p99 target across routes?" -> uncover pain: 'spiky load kills p99'. Demo fallback + routing.
- Initial discovery (for platform team): "How do you currently procure GPU capacity? Is reserved capacity feasible for your org?" -> uncover procurement timing and security blockers. Demo private deployment checklist.

Short demo flow (10 min)
1) 60s product one-liner tailored to persona.
2) 2 min: architecture diagram (hosted vs dedicated vs private).
3) 4 min: live Console demo of the persona hook (eval diff for ML, simulated burst & fallback for backend, private deployment checklist for platform).
4) 2 min: pricing + next steps (POC, pilot scope).

Sample outbound snippets (use short, personalized lines)
- To ML engineer (cold email subject): "Quick: reproduce a model regression in 10 minutes?" Body first line: "Saw your notes on model-drift — we have customers who used our evals UI to find a single prompt that drove a 12% metric drop in production and rolled back in <15m."
- To backend engineer (LinkedIn): "How are you protecting your p99 when routing to LLMs? Built a small simulation for you."
- To platform lead (email): "Reserved inference capacity + compliance checklist — can we map this to your procurement calendar?"

Assets to have on hand for each persona (minimum viable)
- ML engineers: short walk-through video of evals -> rollback, a sample prompt-set report, quickstart repo with a model diff notebook.
- Backend engineers: p99 & cost dashboards screenshots, a small load-test script (k6) tuned to show fallbacks, SDK latency numbers.
- Platform teams: private deployment architecture diagram, KMS/HSM integration doc, reserved capacity pricing sample + TCO spreadsheet.

Battlecard: common objections + one-liners
- "We don't want vendor lock-in." -> "Same API surface across hosted/dedicated/private — you can start hosted and move to private with minimal SDK changes; model pins and rollout configs move with you."
- "OpenAI is simpler." -> "Great for prototypes; Redwood gives you production knobs (batching, cache, dedicated capacity, audit logs) and a predictable runway as usage grows."
- "We manage our own infra." -> "We see teams gain velocity and reduce ops load by using our runtime while keeping strategic control via Private + Dedicated options."

Open questions / hypotheses to validate in next 6 weeks
- Hypothesis A: ML engineers will convert faster if we offer a one-click import of their evaluation prompt sets from existing tools (huggingface/MLFlow).
- Hypothesis B: Backend engineers care more about p99 guarantees than marginal token cost; messaging should surface SLO management up-front.
- Hypothesis C: Platform teams require pre-sales security gating; a 2-page compliance checklist dramatically speeds procurement.
- Action items: build a 1-pager compliance checklist draft (owner: Riley), create a small k6 loadtest repo (owner: Mateo), prototype a prompt-set importer spec (owner: Asha).

Unresolved notes / raw fragments (informal)
- Need updated figures from infra on typical p95/p99 under Dedicated (ask SRE for latest dataset).
- Example customer quote request: ask CS to pull 2 anonymized quotes that mention "reduced p99" or "predictable cost".
- Slack refs: #platform-sales -> thread on reserved-pricing objections, #ml-eng -> prompt-set import ask.

Next steps and owners
- Finalize one-pager artifacts for each persona (Riley due 2026-03-09).
- Create 3 persona-specific demo scripts and short videos (Mateo due 2026-03-16).
- Run 5 targeted discovery calls using these talk tracks and capture win/loss feedback (Asha + GTM team).

Quick revision log
